idea.title: The liking gap
idea.summary: A 2018 psychology study found that after a short chat, strangers liked each other more than each person guessed, which closes on the nerves before a first call.
hookOptions: Strangers like you more than you think
After one chat, they liked you more
Psychologists measured how awkward you feel
sources: Boothby, E. J., Cooney, G., Sandstrom, G. M., & Clark, M. S. (2018). The Liking Gap in Conversations: Do People Like Us More Than We Think? Psychological Science.
Finding: after getting to know a stranger in conversation, people consistently underestimated how much their partner liked them; the researchers named this the liking gap.

scenes.say: After a first chat, people like you more than you think.
In 2018, Erica Boothby and colleagues had strangers chat, then answer questions.
Each person guessed how much the other liked them, and guessed low.
Their partners actually liked them more than they'd guessed.
They named it the liking gap: your worry is louder than their opinion.

scenes.name: Cozy Pickle
scenes.say: So if you're nervous before a first hello, remember the gap.

post.caption:
